notes: Identity verified internally: title Stimulus set size modulates the sex–emotion interaction in face categorization; authors Ottmar V. Lipp, Fika Karnadewi, Belinda M. Craig, Sophie L. Cronin; DOI 10.3758/s13414-015-0849-x; Atten Percept Psychophys (2015) 77:1285–1294. Supplied canonical text is a full primary research article, including methods, results, discussion and references, not an abstract-only parse. No PDF was supplied; no rendering performed. The locator identifies Experiment 1a and the outcome but does not identify expression categorization versus sex categorization. Both are separately analyzed Sex × Expression repeated-measures tests; neither row order nor numeric matching is used to select one. Printed candidates (not assigned): Expression-categorization Sex × Expression response-time interaction: F(1, 23) = 19.73, p < .001, ηp2 = .462. Sex-categorization Sex × Expression response-time interaction: F(1, 23) = 8.79, p = .007, ηp2 = .276. N=24 is only a candidate based on the volunteer count; no N derived from degrees of freedom or stimulus counts. No arithmetic performed. The author verdict is an overall Experiment 1a direct-replication verdict, not an error-specific verdict or a selection of either task. Unassigned original side is a placeholder only.
